Discharge Instructions:
Dear Ms. ___,

You were admitted to the gynecology service after your 
procedure. You have recovered well and the team believes you are 
ready to be discharged home. Please call Dr. ___ 
office with any questions or concerns. Please follow the 
instructions below.

General instructions:
* Take your medications as prescribed.
* Do not drive while taking narcotics.
* Take a stool softener such as colace while taking narcotics to 
prevent constipation.
* Do not combine narcotic and sedative medications or alcohol.
* Do not take more than 4000mg acetaminophen (APAP) in 24 hrs.
* No strenuous activity until your post-op appointment.
* Nothing in the vagina (no tampons, no douching, no sex) for 3 
months
* No heavy lifting of objects >10 lbs for 6 weeks.
* You may eat a regular diet.
* You may walk up and down stairs.

Incision care:
* You may shower and allow soapy water to run over incision; no 
scrubbing of incision. No tub baths for 6 weeks.
* If you have steri-strips, leave them on. They will fall off on 
their own or be removed during your followup visit.

Call your doctor for:
* fever > 100.4F
* severe abdominal pain
* difficulty urinating
* vaginal bleeding requiring >1 pad/hr
* abnormal vaginal discharge
* redness or drainage from incision
* nausea/vomiting where you are unable to keep down fluids/food 
or your medication

To reach medical records to get the records from this 
hospitalization sent to your doctor at home, call ___.

 
Followup Instructions:

History of Present Illness:
___ with H/O hypertension, hyperlipidemia, ? CAD (possible MI in 
the ___, former tobacco use, remote TIA and untreated 
urothelial cell carcinoma who presents with one day of chest 
pain. She began having left sided chest pain on the night prior 
to admission. She described the pain as sharp and located in the 
left chest and going to the shoulder. It was worsened by lying 
flat, better when she got up and walked around. There was no 
associated shortness of breath or nausea. She presented to a 
pain clinic appointment and reported the chest pain in the 
waiting room, so was sent via EMS to the ED. By the time of 
arrival to the ED, she said her pain had resolved, and it has 
not recurred. Of note, at baseline, she walks around her 
apartment, goes to the bank, runs light errands, all without 
chest pain.

In the ED initial vitals were: T 97.8 HR 78 BP 102/68 RR 20 SaO2 
93% on RA. EKG at 1230: NSR, rate 73, ST elevations in II, III, 
aVF, V1-V6. ST depression aVR unchanged from ___. Q waves II, 
III, aVF, V2-V6. ST elevations in III, aVF, and precordial leads 
are more prominent than prior, as are the q waves in precordial 
leads.
1800: Above ST changes are less prominent and more similar to 
___.
Labs/studies notable for: two negative troponin-T 3 hours apart 
at 1200 and 1500. A stat portable echo was performed that did 
not show regional wall motion abnormalities (though windows were 
suboptimal).

Patient was given aspirin, atorvastatin 80 mg (patient unaware 
of prior allergy to atorvastatin) and a heparin gtt. Cardiology 
was consulted and initially was considering coronary 
angiography. According to the ED resident, the patient at first 
was very resistant to going for coronary angiography. Her 
symptoms improved while in the ED, and given absence of wall 
motion abnormalities on TTE and improvement in her symptoms, 
decision was made to manage her medically.

After arrival to the cardiology ward, she denied any chest pain, 
shortness of breath, orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, or 
lower extremity edema.

walking. She denied associated shortness of breath, dyspnea on

not recur. In the emergency department, her EKG showed NSR at a

reports_summary.excerpt:
INDICATION:  ___ year old male w/ bilateral staghorn calculi// PCN placement

COMPARISON:  Noncontrast CT ___

TECHNIQUE:   OPERATORS: Dr. ___, attending Interventional
Radiologist performed the procedure.
ANESTHESIA: Moderate sedation was provided by administrating divided doses of
150mcg of fentanyl and 2.5 mg of midazolam throughout the total intra-service
time of 1 hour 40 minutes during which the patient's hemodynamic parameters
were continuously monitored by an independent trained radiology nurse.  1%
lidocaine was injected in the skin and subcutaneous tissues overlying the
access site.
MEDICATIONS: 1 g ceftriaxone
CONTRAST: 30 ml of Optiray contrast
FLUOROSCOPY TIME AND DOSE:  10 minutes 48 seconds, 56 mGy


PROCEDURE:  1. Right ultrasound guided renal collecting system access.
2. Right nephrostogram.
3. Right 8 ___ nephrostomy tube placement.
4.  Left ultrasound-guided renal collecting system access.
5.  Left nephrostogram.
6.  Left 8 ___ nephrostomy tube placement.

PROCEDURE DETAILS: Following the discussion of the risks, benefits and
alternatives to the procedure, written informed consent was obtained from the
patient. The patient was then brought to the angiography suite and placed
supine on the exam table.  A pre-procedure time-out was performed per ___
protocol.  The right flank was prepped and draped in the usual sterile
fashion.

After the injection of 5 cc of 1% lidocaine in the subcutaneous soft tissues,
the right renal collecting system was accessed through a posterior superior
pole calyx under ultrasound guidance using a 21 gauge Cook needle. Ultrasound
images of the access were stored on PACS. Prompt return of urine confirmed
appropriate positioning. Injection of a small amount of contrast outlined a
dilated renal collecting system. Under fluoroscopic guidance, a Nitinol wire
was advanced into the renal collecting system. After a skin ___, the needle
was exchanged for an Accustick sheath. One the tip of the sheath was in the
collecting system; the sheath was advanced over the wire, inner dilator and
metallic stiffener. The wire and inner dilator were then removed and diluted
contrast was injected into the collecting system to confirm position. A
___ wire was advanced through the sheath and coiled in the collecting
system. The sheath was then removed and an 8 ___ nephrostomy tube was
advanced into the renal collecting system. The wire was then removed and the
pigtail was formed in the collecting system. Contrast injection confirmed
appropriate positioning. The catheter was then flushed, 0 silk stay sutures
applied and the catheter was secured with a Stat Lock device and sterile
dressings. The catheter was attached to a bag.

After the injection of 5 cc of 1% lidocaine in the subcutaneous soft tissues,
the left renal collecting system was accessed through a posterior lower calyx
under ultrasound guidance using a 21 gauge Cook needle.  Prompt return of
urine confirmed appropriate positioning.  Injection of a small amount of
contrast outlined a dilated renal collecting system.  Under fluoroscopic
guidance, a Nitinol wire was advanced into the renal collecting system.  After
a skin ___, the needle was exchanged for an Accustick sheath. Once the tip of
the sheath was in the collecting system; the sheath was advanced over the
wire, inner dilator and metallic stiffner.  The wire and inner dilator were
then removed and diluted contrast was injected into the collecting system to
confirm position.  A ___ wire was advanced through the sheath and coiled
in the collecting system.  The sheath was then removed and an 8 ___
nephrostomy tube was advanced into the renal collecting system.  The wire was
then removed and the pigtail was formed. Contrast injection confirmed
appropriate positioning. The catheter was then flushed, 0 silk stay sutures
applied and the catheter was secured with a Stat Lock device and sterile
dressings. The catheter was attached to a bag.

FINDINGS: 

Initial ultrasound images of the right kidney demonstrate multiple fluid
filled lobulations with layering hyperechoic material likely dilated calices
with debris though could be milk of calcium cysts.  A superior calyx was
chosen for access as it could be directly traced to the renal collecting
system by ultrasound.  Extremely thin and atrophic parenchyma was noted
throughout the entire right kidney.

Initial contrast injection into the right kidney demonstrated filling of a
superior pole calyx and the renal pelvis to the level of an obstructing stone
at the UPJ.  Subsequently, hypoechoic fluid was noted to be outside the renal
parenchyma by ultrasound imaging following contrast injection of 6 cc
suggesting forniceal rupture.

Successful placement of an 8 ___ percutaneous nephrostomy tube with
aspiration of a large volume of thick milky sediment which could represent
calcific debris or pus.  A sample was sent for culture.  Pink tinged urine
output was noted following initial access with significant debris draining
into the drainage bag.

Initial ultrasound images of the left kidney demonstrate marked hydronephrosis
with layering debris.  Extremely thin and atrophic parenchyma was noted
throughout the entire left kidney.

Initial contrast injection through the left kidney access demonstrated filling
of lower pole calices and a large obstructing caps stone within the renal
pelvis.

Successful placement of an 8 ___ percutaneous nephrostomy tube with a small
volume of milky sediment appreciated.  A sample was sent for culture.  Pink
tinged urine output was noted following initial access with some debris
draining into the drainage bag.

IMPRESSION: 

Successful placement of bilateral 8 ___ nephrostomy tubes.

Bilateral milky sediment sent for culture.  Suspect calcific debris though
would like to exclude infection.

RECOMMENDATION(S):  Future plans for percutaneous lithotripsy by urology.

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with heart failure, s/p fall with ?syncope,
found to have elevated d-dimer.  // assess for PE

TECHNIQUE:  Axial multidetector CT images were obtained through the thorax
after the uneventful administration of 100 cc of Omnipaque intravenous
contrast.
Reformatted coronal, sagittal, thin slice axial images, and oblique maximal
intensity projection images were submitted to PACS and reviewed.

DOSE:  DLP: 455 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  CT chest performed ___.

FINDINGS: 

The thyroid appears somewhat heterogeneous in attenuation though no focal
nodule is identified.  There is no axillary, supraclavicular, mediastinal, or
hilar adenopathy.  A left chest pacer is identified, is please which terminate
in the right atrium and right ventricle.

The heart is enlarged and stable in size.  There is a small pericardial
effusion, which relative to prior study performed ___ is new. 
The ascending aorta is non aneurysmal and measures 3.4 cm in size.  The
pulmonary artery is within normal limits in caliber.  Coronary artery
calcifications are moderate and most pronounced within the left anterior
descending artery.  The atrium bilaterally appear enlarged.

The pulmonary artery is opacified to the subsegmental level.  There is no
filling defect to suggest a pulmonary embolism.

Respiratory motion somewhat limits evaluation of the lungs.  New bilateral
layering and nonhemorrhagic pleural effusions are small.  Dependent
ground-glass opacities and interlobular septal thickening is mild.  Bibasilar
atelectasis is moderate.  There is no mass, consolidation, or suspicious
nodule.

Although not tailored for subdiaphragmatic evaluation, imaged portions of the
liver and spleen are unremarkable.  Partially imaged bilateral adrenal
myelolipoma is noted (02:10 2).

Osseous structures demonstrates no suspicious lytic or blastic lesion. 
Multilevel degenerative changes are mild.

IMPRESSION: 

1.  No evidence of pulmonary embolism.
2.  Cardiomegaly, bilateral nonhemorrhagic layering pleural effusions, and
dependent ground-glass opacities with interlobular septal thickening
consistent with findings of congestive heart failure.
3. Stable appearance of partially imaged bilateral adrenal myelolipoma.

EXAMINATION:  CT C-SPINE W/O CONTRAST

INDICATION:  ___ with head strike on blood thinners and neck pain  // bleed or
neck fx?

TECHNIQUE:  Non-contrast helical multidetector CT was performed.Soft tissue
and bone algorithm images were generated.  Coronal and sagittal reformations
were then constructed.

DOSE:  Total DLP (Body) = 733 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  CT chest dated ___.
CT C-spine dated ___.
Chest radiograph dated ___ at 20:55.

FINDINGS: 

There is unchanged 2 mm of anterolisthesis C3 on C4 and 2mm of anterolithesis
of C4 on C5.  No fracture is identified.  There is no prevertebral soft tissue
swelling.  There are degenerative changes consisting of intervertebral disc
space narrowing, anterior osteophyte formation, vacuum space phenomena,
endplate sclerosis and cystic formation, posterior intervertebral osteophyte
formation most conspicuous from C2 through C7.  Superior endplate focal
depression and irregularity of T1 is unchanged.  Posterior intervertebral
osteophytes do encroach on the spinal canal, however there is no severe
stenosis, within the limitations of CT.

The thyroid has a stable right lower lobe 7 mm nodule.  There is a
moderate-sized pleural effusion on the right, as seen on chest radiograph
completed same day.  There is a small left pleural effusion.  Subcutaneous
nodule in the left occipital soft tissues is likely sebaceous cyst.  The right
submandibular gland has been removed.

IMPRESSION:


1. No fracture or traumatic malalignment.
2. Multilevel multifactorial degenerative changes most conspicuous from C2
through C7.
3. Partially imaged layering bilateral effusions, larger on the right.

EXAMINATION:  CT HEAD W/O CONTRAST

INDICATION:  ___ with head strike on blood thinners and neck pain.

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous axial images of the brain were obtained without
contrast. Coronal and sagittal reformations as well as bone algorithm
reconstructions were provided and reviewed.

DOSE:  Total DLP (Head) = 803 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  CT head dated ___ at 22:22.

FINDINGS: 

There is no evidence of acute major territorial infarction, hemorrhage, edema,
or large mass. The ventricles and sulci are prominent, consistent with age
related volume loss.  Periventricular and deep white matter hypodensities
while nonspecific likely represent the sequelae of chronic small vessel
disease.

There is no evidence of fracture.  There is mucosal thickening in the ethmoids
air cells and left maxillary sinus.  The visualized portion of the orbits are
unremarkable.  Left occipital subcutaneous tissue is likely a sebaceous cyst.

IMPRESSION: 

No acute intracranial process.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ year old male who presented with back pain, 
fatigue, and significant weight loss, subsequently found to have 
multiple lesions of the spine, skull, and brain concerning for 
metastatic malignancy.

# Metastatic malignancy, unknown primary: On this admission, 
patient presented with significant radicular back pain in the 
setting of weight loss and continued fatigue. Patient was assess 
for his back pain with imaging, which was notable for metastatic 
disease burden, with multiple soft tissue and bony lesions 
involving the spine, liver, brain, lung and multiple bone 
locations identified. Patient underwent an uncomplicated Right 
pelvic biopsy on ___, and tissue was sent for pathological 
analysis. Initial pathology was notable for malignant cells, 
likely adenocarcinoma. Final pathology was notable for carcinoma 
strongly positive for CK7, positive for CDX2, and negative for 
CK20, PAX8, and TTF-1, which although not specific, was 
suggestive of a pancreaticobiliary,  upper GI or colorectal 
origin. An EGD was performed on this admission which was was 
unremarkable for a notable GI mass. PET CT was notable for 
extensive FDG avid metastatic disease throughout the bilateral 
lungs, mediastinum, right hilum, liver, left gluteal 
musculature, and osseous structures, with nodefinitive primary 
malignancy identified by PET. However, based on patients 
distribution of disease with significant pulmonary disease 
burden including a 4.2cm right suprahilar mass obstructing the 
SVC and innumerable pulmonary metastases in all lobes (larges in 
RLL up to 1.9cm) and relatively little GI involvement (hepatic 
lesions were noted to be like harmatomas rather than metastatic 
disease), concern remained high for a primary lung cancer with 
lung adenocarcinoma being a likely candidate to explain patients 
presentation and metastatic disease burden. Due to patients 
multiple spinal mets, patient was assessed by ortho spine who 
noted patient could remain weight bearing as tolerated. Due to 
patients extensive brain metastases, patient was assessed by 
radiation oncology, and plan was made for patient to receive 
WBRT. Patient received 5 treatments of WBRT, which he tolerated 
well. Patients R thigh was also treated with 5 doses of XRT 
external beam radiation as this was a focus of significant pain 
for patient and had bony met involvement. Following treatment 
with WBRT, patient required XRT to spine from T1 to T8 due to 
progressive metastatic disease with concern for cord impingement 
(see below). Despite being a TTF-1 negative staining indicating 
a non-lung process, plan was made to approach patients cancer as 
adenocarcinoma of unknown primary vs non-small cell lung 
carcinoma, with plan for followup in thoracic oncology  
following acute rehab to improve strength and mobility. 

#T1 vertebral body erosion into spinal canal/bony mets: During 
this admission, patient was noted to have T1 met which had 
eroded into the spinal canal, with  extra cortical soft tissue 
extension at T1, T8 and L4 vertebral bodies with encroachment to 
the epidural space without resultant high-grade sinal canal 
narrowing or cord impingement. Due to notable mets with concern 
for progressive disease causing cord compression/spinal canal 
narrowing, patient was planned for 5 doses of XRT to the T1 to 
T8 spine. Patient tolerated this treatment well, with marked 
improvement in his back pain. Patient completed his 5 planned 
doses of XRT prior to discharge to rehab, and was further given

patient presented with significant radicular back pain in the 
setting of weight loss and continued fatigue. Patient was assess 
for his back pain with imaging, which was notable for metastatic 
disease burden, with multiple soft tissue and bony lesions 
involving the spine, liver, brain, lung and multiple bone 
locations identified. Patient underwent an uncomplicated Right 
pelvic biopsy on ___, and tissue was sent for pathological 
analysis. Initial pathology was notable for malignant cells, 
likely adenocarcinoma. Final pathology was notable for carcinoma 
strongly positive for CK7, positive for CDX2, and negative for 
CK20, PAX8, and TTF-1, which although not specific, was 
suggestive of a pancreaticobiliary,  upper GI or colorectal 
origin. An EGD was performed on this admission which was was 
unremarkable for a notable GI mass. PET CT was notable for 
extensive FDG avid metastatic disease throughout the bilateral 
lungs, mediastinum, right hilum, liver, left gluteal 
musculature, and osseous structures, with nodefinitive primary 
malignancy identified by PET. However, based on patients 
distribution of disease with significant pulmonary disease 
burden including a 4.2cm right suprahilar mass obstructing the 
SVC and innumerable pulmonary metastases in all lobes (larges in 
RLL up to 1.9cm) and relatively little GI involvement (hepatic 
lesions were noted to be like harmatomas rather than metastatic 
disease), concern remained high for a primary lung cancer with 
lung adenocarcinoma being a likely candidate to explain patients 
presentation and metastatic disease burden. Due to patients 
multiple spinal mets, patient was assessed by ortho spine who 
noted patient could remain weight bearing as tolerated. Due to 
patients extensive brain metastases, patient was assessed by 
radiation oncology, and plan was made for patient to receive 
WBRT. Patient received 5 treatments of WBRT, which he tolerated

eroded into the spinal canal, with  extra cortical soft tissue

narrowing, patient was planned for 5 doses of XRT to the T1 to

improvement in his back pain. Patient completed his 5 planned

breakdown

reports_summary.excerpt:
EXAMINATION:  CTU without contrast followed by with contrast

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with metastatic adenocarcinoma of uncertain
primary with diffuse lung and spine metastasis, demonstrated to have new R
hydroureteronephrosis on MRI. // Please eval new R hydroureteronephrosis

TECHNIQUE:  Single phase split bolus contrast: MDCT axial images were acquired
through the abdomen and pelvis following intravenous contrast administration
with split bolus technique.
Oral contrast was administered.
Coronal and sagittal reformations were performed and reviewed on PACS.

DOSE:  Acquisition sequence: 1) Spiral Acquisition 8.5 s, 55.4 cm; CTDIvol =
3.6 mGy (Body) DLP = 198.8 mGy-cm. 2) Sequenced Acquisition 0.5 s, 0.2 cm;
CTDIvol = 9.3 mGy (Body) DLP = 1.9 mGy-cm. 3) Stationary Acquisition 1.2 s,
0.2 cm; CTDIvol = 20.0 mGy (Body) DLP = 4.0 mGy-cm. 4) Spiral Acquisition 8.5
s, 55.4 cm; CTDIvol = 7.9 mGy (Body) DLP = 432.9 mGy-cm. Total DLP (Body) =
638 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  MRI thoracic and lumbar PT6 MR spine from ___ CT
abdomen pelvis with contrast from ___ PET-CT from ___

FINDINGS: 

LOWER CHEST: Multiple pulmonary nodules are re-demonstrated in the lung bases.
Small right pleural effusion from previous film has resolved.  Mild
subsegmental atelectasis seen at right lung base.  No pericardial effusion
seen.

ABDOMEN:

HEPATOBILIARY: There are multiple hypodense lesions within the liver, overall
still too small to characterize, but likely representing biliary hamartomas
versus less likely metastases or cysts.  The largest hypodense lesion seen we
identified in segment 2 has remained stable at 1.7 cm.  There is no evidence
of intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary dilatation. The gallbladder is within
normal limits.

PANCREAS: The pancreas has normal attenuation throughout, without evidence of
focal lesions or pancreatic ductal dilatation.  There is no peripancreatic
stranding.

SPLEEN: The spleen shows normal size and attenuation throughout, without
evidence of focal lesions.

ADRENALS: Bilateral adrenal nodules, likely malignant, noted, which is
consistent with recent PET-CT.

URINARY: The kidneys are of normal and symmetric size with normal nephrogram.
There is a 1.3 cm cyst that is reidentified in the right mid to lower kidney. 
There are no focal lesions of the left kidney.  .  There is no perinephric
abnormality.  No hydronephrosis is appreciated bilaterally.

GASTROINTESTINAL: The stomach is unremarkable. Small bowel loops demonstrate
normal caliber, wall thickness, and enhancement throughout.  The colon and
rectum are within normal limits.  The appendix is not visualized.

PELVIS: The urinary bladder is distended, and appears otherwise unremarkable. 
There is no free fluid in the pelvis.

LYMPH NODES:  Peripherally calcified lymph node in left lower quadrant
re-identified and stable.

VASCULAR: There is no abdominal aortic aneurysm. Femoral port noted on left.

BONES AND SOFT TISSUES: Multiple lytic and sclerotic lesions within the
thoracolumbar spine and pelvis.  Permeative lesion in L4 vertebral body with
associated pathological fracture re-demonstrated.  A destructive lesion of the
right acetabulum is demonstrated with associated soft tissue component which
extends towards the right obturator internus muscle.  Left gluteus medius soft
tissue mass, consistent with recent PET-CT reidentified.

Please see recent PET-CT scan for best appreciation of multiple bony and soft
tissue masses.

IMPRESSION:


1. No hydronephrosis.
2. Multiple bony and soft tissue masses, best appreciated on recent PET-CT
from ___.
3. Bilateral adrenal masses, c/w metastases.
4. Multiple stable pulmonary nodules in the lung bases. Small right pleural
effusion from previous film has resolved.
5. Multiple liver hypoattenuations likely hamartomas versus less likely
metastases.
6. Right renal cyst.

EXAMINATION:  MRI THORACIC AND LUMBAR PT6 MR SPINE

INDICATION:  History of metastatic cancer, likely lung adenocarcinoma with new
finding of T1 vertebral body lesion with possible erosion into the spinal
canal.

TECHNIQUE:  Sagittal imaging was performed with T2, T1, and STIR technique. 
Axial T2 imaging was performed. Axial GRE images of the cervical spine were
performed.  After the uneventful administration of 8 mL of Gadavist contrast
agent, additional axial and sagittal T1 images were obtained.

COMPARISON:  CT neck ___.  Whole-body PET-CT ___.  Total spine
MR ___

FINDINGS: 

THORACIC:
Again, there are numerous T1 hypointense T2 hyperintense enhancing lesions
throughout the thoracic spine compatible with diffuse osseous metastatic
disease, as seen on the recent prior MR examination from ___.  There
is diffuse involvement of the T1 vertebral body with extension into the right
pedicle and facet with extra cortical extension into the epidural space at the
level the right pedicle by about 3 mm (18:3).  Another area of involvement is
within the T8 vertebral body where a rounded lesion in the vertebral body
measuring 17 mm has increased in size, previously 15 mm and there is extension
and expansion of the right pedicle and facet, now with further expansion and
with involvement of the spinous process.  There is extra cortical extension
into the epidural space, shifting the cord the left causing mild canal
stenosis at this level without impingement.  There is extension of roughly 6
mm into the epidural space (19:36).  Involvement from T9 through T12 has also
progressed compared to the prior examination, in particular the superior left
aspect of the T12 vertebral body where a smaller lesions have now coalesced
into a larger lesion measuring at least 33 x 15 mm.  Vertebral body heights
are otherwise maintained without evidence of pathologic fracture degenerative
changes appear similar to the ___ examination.  Spinal cord signal
and morphology is normal.

LUMBAR:  Again seen are areas of marrow placement with the post gadolinium
enhancement in the L1, L4, L5 and S3 vertebral bodies.  At L1, multiple
lesions are seen coalescing at the left aspect of the superior vertebral body
which appears increased compared to the prior examination, for example at the
anterior superior endplate 18 x 16 mm lesion previously measured 14 x 12 mm. 
Again, there is extension into the left pedicle and facet and another rounded
lesion is seen at the spinous process at this level measuring 12 x 10 mm,
previously 6 x 6 mm (12:11).  Again, there is diffuse involvement of the L4
vertebral body with extension to the bilateral pedicles which appears
progressed, with further extension of the right pedicle with probable trace
soft tissue extension into the anterior epidural space.  There is also
prevertebral soft tissue enhancement appearing similar to the prior
examination likely representing cortical breakthrough.  8 mm lesion in the
posterior aspect of the L3 vertebral body is new.  There is also involvement
of the left L5 pedicle and facet as well as the posterior superior endplate
which appears mildly progressed compared the prior examination.

Scattered degenerative changes appears similar to the prior examination. 
Again seen is a fracture line parallel to the superior endplate of the L4
vertebral body with minimal superior endplate compression though the remainder
of the vertebral body height is relatively well maintained.  Spinal cord
signal and morphology is normal.

OTHER: There is a 1.2 cm right interpolar renal cyst.  Mild right
hydroureteronephrosis is new and is not fully characterize.  Several punctate
T2 hyperintense liver lesions are partially visualized.  Several enhancing
lung lesions are partially visualized, measuring up to 1.9 cm with spiculation
in the right lung base.

IMPRESSION:


1. Progressive osseous metastatic disease, as described in detail above.

and ultimately transitioned to PO Torsemide.  During

weaned off dobutamine as above.

performed with gradient echo, FLAIR, diffusion, and T1 technique. Sagittal
MPRAGE imaging was performed and re-formatted in axial and coronal

The study is mildly degraded by motion somewhat limiting the evaluation.

or infarction.   The ventricles and sulci are patent and prominent in keeping
with age-related volume loss.  There is no abnormal enhancement after contrast
administration.

Few scattered foci of T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the periventricular and

ischemic disease.

There is a focus of susceptibility in the inferior right frontal lobe on image
14:  12, likely secondary to prior microhemorrhage.

The orbits are unremarkable.  Mild mucosal thickening in bilateral ethmoid air
cells and bilateral maxillary sinuses.  The remaining visualized paranasal
sinuses and mastoid air cells are clear.  Intracranial flow voids are
maintained.

IMPRESSION:


1. No acute intracranial abnormality.
2. No abnormal enhancement on postcontrast images to suggest intracranial
metastasis from patient's lung cancer.
3. Right frontal focus of chronic hemorrhage

PROCEDURE:  CT-guided lung biopsy.

OPERATORS:  Dr. ___ resident, Dr. ___ fellow, and
Dr. ___ radiologist. Dr. ___ supervised the trainee
during the key components of the procedure and reviewed and agrees with the
trainee's findings.

TECHNIQUE:  The risks, benefits, and alternatives of the procedure were
explained to the patient.  After a detailed discussion, informed written
consent was obtained.  A pre-procedure timeout using three patient identifiers
was performed per ___ protocol.

The patient was placed in a supine position on the CT scan table.  Limited
preprocedure CTscan of the intended biopsy area was performed.  Based on the
CT findings an appropriate position for the biopsy was chosen.  The site was
marked.

The site was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.  1% lidocaine
were administered to the subcutaneous for local anesthetic effect.  Deep
anesthetic was not given due to minimal subcutaneous tissue.  Under CT
guidance, a 17 gauge coaxial needle was introduced into the lesion.  An 18
gauge core biopsy device with a 22 mm throw was used to obtain 2 core biopsy
specimens which contained significant necrotic tissue.  Subsequently, the
needle was repositioned with tip pointing anteriorly at a more solid component
within the mass and 2 additional core biopsy specimens were obtained.  Biopsy
specimens were sent for pathology.  Afterwards an additional core biopsy was
obtained with tip pointing anteriorly which was sent for microbiology.

The specimen was evaluated by onsite cytologist, deemed adequate.

The procedure was tolerated well and there were no immediate post-procedural
complications.

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with ESRD ___ T2DM s/p DCDRT in ___, idiopathic
pHTN, recently diagnosed Stage 3a SCC of Lung, admitted for 10 pound weight
loss, hypotension, malaise, chest pressure, productive cough and now fever
while in hospital. Currently s/p 3 doses of taxol/carboplatin and 18
mediastinal and lung radiation therapy tx.  // assess for interval change in

TECHNIQUE:   Multi detector helical scanning of the chest was reconstructed as
5 and 1.25 mm thick axial, 2.5 mm thick coronal and parasagittal, and 8 mm MIP
axial images.  Contrast agent was not administered. All images were reviewed.
DOSAGE:  TOTAL DLP ___

COMPARISON:  Chest CT scanning since ___, most recently ___.

FINDINGS: 

In the absence of intravenous contrast or subcutaneous and central fat to
define tissue planes, assessment of borderline lymph node enlargement, such as
assessing the stability of bilateral sub cm supraclavicular nodes is not
possible.  There are no soft tissue abnormalities in the chest wall suspicious
for malignancy.

This study is not appropriate for subdiaphragmatic evaluation.  Adrenals are
not clearly displayed.  Right kidney is atrophic.

What was a large fluid filled mediastinal structure extending from the right
upper paratracheal station in the prevascular plane to the intra pericardial
right pulmonary artery has increased in attenuation, probably due to
increasing exudate or blood mixed in the fluid, but it is smaller today. 
Inferiorly it abuts possible new mild small pericardial effusion is stable. 
Moderate dependent, nonhemorrhagic left pleural effusion is larger and has an
slight increase in apical component.  Mild lymph node enlargement in the right
paratracheal station and origin of the right hilus.  Cm size left lower
paratracheal nodes are unchanged.  7 mm prevascular mediastinal node, 5:100 24
is also stable.  Hilar contours do not suggest substantial adenopathy and
there is no narrowing of the bronchi.

Ascending thoracic aorta is top-normal size.  Descending thoracic aorta is
generally dilated, maximum diameter 40 mm, unchanged.  Calcification conforms
to pseudo intima along the inner margin of the large mural thrombus documented
on chest CTA ___.  Atherosclerotic coronary calcification
involves at least the LAD.

Dilatation of the intra pericardial right pulmonary artery, 29 mm, is
unchanged.  Hypoattenuation of cardiac contents reflects anemia.

Course pleural parenchymal nodularity traversed by dilated bronchi at both
lung apices is largely scarring, but more nodular components would warrant
surveillance to exclude malignancy, particularly a 10 mm wide pleural-based
lung nodule, 5:70, unchanged since ___.  .  Similarly, this nodularity
may encase a small region of lung simulating a 15 mm cavity, 05:55, not
appreciably changed since ___ and not containing fluid or associated with
bronchiectasis or other findings of active infection.

Large mass, 50 by 58 mm, previously 43 x 57 mm at the base of the left lung
extends from thickened costal pleura to the pleura of the diaphragm and the
mediastinum along the pericardium and left ventricle.  It is heterogeneous,
partially cavitated, partially fluid containing, presumably necrotic
bronchogenic carcinoma, but conceivably superinfected.

There are no bone lesions in the chest wall suspicious for malignancy.  .




IMPRESSION: 

Growing necrotic left lower lobe mass responsible for increasing left pleural
effusion could be superinfected.

Large mediastinal cyst or pericardial diverticulum, has turned exudative or
hemorrhagic.

Suspicious nodules difficult to separate from marked nodular biapical
scarring.  CT surveillance recommended, as determined by clinical
circumstances.

Probable pulmonary arterial hypertension.

Anemia.

Grossly stable ___ to large, fusiform, previously demonstrated aneurysm
descending thoracic aorta.  The condition of the aortic lumen is not addressed
by this study.

Coronary atherosclerosis.

INDICATION:  post-op with intra-op femoral shaft fracture  // post-op with
intra-op femoral shaft fracture

COMPARISON:  Radiographs from ___

IMPRESSION: 

There is a right bipolar hemiarthroplasty. There is a long stem femoral
component with cerclage wires along the femoral shaft.  2 cortical screws are
seen within the distal femoral shaft fixating an oblique fracture of the
distal femoral shaft.  The fracture line is seen exiting the medial femoral
cortex distally.  No hardware related complications are seen.  No significant
changes seen from prior.

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with malignant neoplasm of connective aand soft
tissue  // please place SL port.  pt to be admitted for chemo, please schedure
for AM thank you, ___

COMPARISON:  Chest CT ___.

TECHNIQUE:  OPERATORS: Dr. ___ and Dr.
___ radiologist performed the procedure. Dr. ___
supervised the trainee during the key components of the procedure and has
reviewed and agrees with the trainee's findings.
ANESTHESIA: Moderate sedation was provided by administrating divided doses of
150 mcg of fentanyl and 2 mg of midazolam throughout the total intra-service
time of 30 minutes during which the patient's hemodynamic parameters were
continuously monitored by an independent trained radiology nurse. 1% lidocaine
was injected in the skin and subcutaneous tissues overlying the access site.
MEDICATIONS:  1 g ancef, 150 mcg fentanyl, 2 mg versed.
CONTRAST: 0 ml of Optiray contrast.
FLUOROSCOPY TIME AND DOSE:  0:29 min, 33 cGy.cm2

PROCEDURE
1. Right internal jugular approach chest single lumen Port-a-cath placement

PROCEDURE DETAILS: Following the explanation of the risks, benefits and
alternatives to the procedure, written informed consent was obtained from the
patient. The patient was then brought to the angiography suite and placed
supine on the exam table. A pre-procedure time-out was performed per ___
protocol. The upper chest was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.
Under continuous ultrasound guidance, the patent right internal jugular vein
was compressible and accessed using a micropuncture needle. Permanent
ultrasound images were obtained before and after intravenous access, which
confirmed vein patency. Subsequently a Nitinol wire was passed into the right
atrium using fluoroscopic guidance. The needle was exchanged for a
micropuncture sheath. The Nitinol wire was removed and a short ___ wire was
advanced to make appropriate measurements for catheter length. The ___ wire
was then passed distally into the IVC.
Next, attention was turned towards creation of a subcutaneous pocket over the
upper anterior chest wall. After instilling superficial and deeper local
anesthesia using lidocaine mixed with epinephrine, a 2.5 cm transverse
incision was made and a subcutaneous pocket was created by using blunt
dissection. The single lumen port was then connected to the catheter.  The
catheter was tunneled from the subcutaneous pocket towards the venotomy site
from where it was brought out using a tunneling device. The port was then
connected to the catheter and checks were made for any leakage by accessing
the diaphragm using a non-coring ___ needle. No leaks were found.
The port was then placed in the subcutaneous pocket and secured with ___
prolene sutures on either side. The venotomy tract was dilated using the
introducer of the peel-away sheath supplied. Following this, the peel-away
sheath was placed over the ___ wire through which the port was threaded into
the right side of the heart with the tip in the right atrium.  The sheath was
then peeled away.
The subcutaneous pocket was closed in layers with ___ interrupted and ___
subcuticular continuous Vicryl sutures.  Steri-strips were used to close the
venotomy incision site. Steri-Strips were applied over the sutures. Final spot
fluoroscopic image demonstrating good alignment of the catheter and no
kinking. The tip is in the right atrium.
The port was accessed using a non coring ___ needle and could be aspirated
and flushed easily. Sterile dressings were applied. The patient tolerated the
procedure well without immediate complication.  The port was left accessed as
requested.

FINDINGS: 

Patent right internal jugular vein. Final fluoroscopic image showing port with
catheter tip terminating in the right atrium.

IMPRESSION: 

Successful placement of a single lumen chest power Port-a-cath via the right
internal jugular venous approach. The tip of the catheter terminates in the
right atrium. The catheter is ready for use.

TECHNIQUE:  OPERATORS: Dr. ___, Interventional Radiology Fellow and Dr.
___, attending radiologist performed the procedure. Dr. ___
personally supervised the trainee during the key components of the procedure
and has reviewed and agrees with the trainee's findings.
ANESTHESIA: Moderate sedation was provided by administrating divided doses of
50mcg of fentanyl and 1 mg of midazolam throughout the total intra-service
time of 20 during which the patient's hemodynamic parameters were continuously
monitored by an independent trained radiology nurse. 1% lidocaine was injected
in the skin and subcutaneous tissues overlying the access site.
MEDICATIONS: Fentanyl, Versed
CONTRAST: 40 ml of Optiray contrast.
FLUOROSCOPY TIME AND DOSE:  2 min, 13 mGy

PROCEDURE:
1. IVC venogram.
2. Infrarenal Denali IVC filter deployment.
3. Post-filter placement venogram.

PROCEDURE DETAILS: Following the discussion of the risks, benefits and
alternatives to the procedure, written informed consent was obtained from the
patient. The patient was then brought to the angiography suite and placed
supine on the exam table. A pre-procedure time-out was performed per ___
protocol. the right neck was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.
Under ultrasound and fluoroscopic guidance, the patent and compressible Right
internal jugular vein was punctured using a 21G micropuncture needle.
Ultrasound images of the access was stored on PACS. A ___ wire was
advanced through the micropuncture sheath into the inferior vena cava. A 8
___ sheath was exchanged for the micropuncture sheath and advanced into the
IVC. An inferior vena cava venogram was performed.

Based on the results of the venogram, detailed below, a decision was made to
place a infrarenal filter. The catheter and sheath were removed over the wire
and the sheath of an Denali filter was advanced over the wire into the IVC
past the take-off of the renal vessels. An inferior vena cava filter was
advanced over the wire until the cranial tip was at the level of the inferior
margin of the lower renal vein. The sheath was then withdrawn until the filter
was deployed. The wire and loading device were then removed through the sheath
and a repeat contrast injection was performed, confirming appropriate filter
positioning. The final image was stored on PACS.
The sheath was removed and pressure was held for 10 minutes,at which point
hemostasis was achieved. A sterile dressing was applied.
The patient tolerated the procedure well and there were no immediate post
procedure complications.

FINDINGS:


1. Patent normal sized, non-duplicated IVC with single bilateral renal veins
and no evidence of a clot.
2. Successful deployment of an infra-renal Denali IVC filter.

    and a repeat contrast injection was performed, confirming appropriate filter
    positioning. The final image was stored on PACS.

    hemostasis was achieved. A sterile dressing was applied.

INDICATION:  ___ RLE sarcoma metastatic to lung, now with large RLE bleed  //
Assess for source of bleeding, and also any progression in lung lesions. Metal

mGy-cm.
 Total DLP (Body) = 1,932 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  PET-CT dated ___, CT chest dated ___

FINDINGS: 

VASCULAR:

There is no abdominal aortic aneurysm.  There is extensive calcium burden in
the abdominal aorta and great abdominal arteries.

CHEST:  Evaluation of the chest wall shows no evidence of supraclavicular,
axillary, or cervical lymphadenopathy.  An enhancing lesion is seen in the
left lobe of the thyroid.

The heart is normal in appearance.  The aorta is normal in caliber.  Again
noted is eccentric filling defect within a right lower lobe pulmonary artery,
consistent with chronic embolus, unchanged since ___.

In the right lower lobe, again seen is a pulmonary nodule, suspicious for
metastasis, measuring 1.2 cm in greatest dimension, previously 0.7 cm.  A
millimetric nodule in the left lower lobe has remained stable since the prior
examination (06:43).  Another left lower lobe nodule (06:40), has developed,
new since the prior examination.  Multiple apical subpleural nodules seem to
have remained stable.

The airways are patent to the subsegmental level.

ABDOMEN:

HEPATOBILIARY: The liver demonstrates homogenous attenuation throughout. There
is no evidence of focal lesions. There is no evidence of intrahepatic or
extrahepatic biliary dilatation.  The gallbladder is within normal limits,
without stones or gallbladder wall thickening.

PANCREAS: The pancreas has normal attenuation throughout, without evidence of
focal lesions or pancreatic ductal dilatation. There is no peripancreatic
stranding.

SPLEEN: The spleen is enlarged, and measures 15.6 cm, and demonstrates
heterogeneous enhancement.

ADRENALS: The adrenal glands are somewhat nodular, unchanged since the prior
examination.

URINARY: The kidneys are of normal and symmetric size with normal nephrogram. 
A hypodense lesion in the upper pole of the left kidney is noted, with an
apparent enhancing septation.  There is no hydronephrosis.  No obstructive
calculi are identified.  There are no urothelial lesions in the kidneys or
ureters. There is no perinephric abnormality.

GASTROINTESTINAL: Small bowel loops demonstrate normal caliber, wall thickness
and enhancement throughout. Colon and rectum are within normal limits.  Though
the appendix is not definitively visualized, there are no secondary signs of
appendicitis.  There is no evidence of mesenteric lymphadenopathy.

RETROPERITONEUM: There is no evidence of retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy.

PELVIS: The urinary bladder and distal ureters are unremarkable.  Again noted
is an enlarged right external iliac lymph node, it now measuring 5.4 x 3.4 cm,
previously 3.1 x 2.6 cm.  There is no free fluid in the pelvis.

REPRODUCTIVE ORGANS: The visualized reproductive organs are unremarkable.

BONES: There is no evidence of worrisome osseous lesions or acute fracture. 
The patient has undergone prior right total hip arthroplasty.

SOFT TISSUES: Again noted is a large hematoma along the right lateral body,
which extends to the mid/ distal femur.  Evaluation for active extravasation
is severely limited given significant metallic artifact from total right hip
arthroplasty.  No definite active extravasation is noted.  Approximate
dimension measure 10 x 8 x 30 cm.  Malignant involvement of this region is
difficult to assess, given metallic artifact and large hematoma.  .

IMPRESSION:


1. Extensive hematoma involving the right lateral thigh to at least the level
of the mid femur.  Within the limitations of the examination given beam
hardening artifact from the right hip prosthesis, no definite active bleeding
is identified.
2. Enlarging right external iliac lymph node.
3. New and enlarging pulmonary nodules.
4. Chronic right lower lobe pulmonary embolus.

EXAMINATION:  ABDOMEN US (COMPLETE STUDY)

INDICATION:  ___ man with CKD, high grade unclassified sarcoma
(malignant fibrous histiocytoma) of the right femur status post radical
resection in ___ with adjuvant chemotherapy now found of local
recurrence and pulmonary nodules, complicated by hematoma, with persistent
anemia, evaluate for retroperitoneal bleed, splenomegaly, portal vein
thrombus.

TECHNIQUE:  Grey scale and color Doppler ultrasound images of the abdomen were
obtained.

COMPARISON:
1. CTA chest ___.
2. Renal ultrasound ___.

FINDINGS: 

LIVER: The hepatic parenchyma appears within normal limits. The contour of the
liver is smooth. There is no focal liver mass. The main portal vein is patent
with hepatopetal flow. There is no ascites.

BILE DUCTS: There is no intrahepatic biliary dilation. The CBD measures 4 mm.

GALLBLADDER: There is no evidence of stones or gallbladder wall thickening.

PANCREAS: Imaged portion of the pancreas appears within normal limits, without
masses or pancreatic ductal dilation, with portions of the pancreatic tail
obscured by overlying bowel gas.

SPLEEN: Normal echogenicity, measuring 13.0 cm.

KIDNEYS: The right kidney measures 9.9 cm. The left kidney measures 10.5 cm.
Normal cortical echogenicity and corticomedullary differentiation is seen
bilaterally.  In the left upper pole renal cortex there is a 1.3 cm simple
renal cyst.  There is no evidence of concerning solid renal mass, stones, or
hydronephrosis in the kidneys.

RETROPERITONEUM: Visualized portions of aorta and IVC are within normal
limits.

IMPRESSION: 

Unremarkable abdominal ultrasound.  Top normal spleen size (13.0 cm).  Patent
portal vein with normal direction of flow.  Note, ultrasound is not sensitive
for the detection of retroperitoneal hematoma.

EXAMINATION:  CTA LOWER EXT W/ANDW/O C AND RECONS RIGHT

INDICATION:  ___ w/swelling to proximal right thigh, hx of osteosarcoma with
resection, with right hip replacement, please eval for active extravasation
into proximal right thigh

TECHNIQUE:  Right lower extremity CTA: Non-contrast and arterial phase
post-contrast images were acquired through the right thigh.
Oral contrast was not administered.
MIP reconstructions were performed on independent workstation and reviewed on
PACS.

DOSE:  Acquisition sequence:
   1) Spiral Acquisition 11.6 s, 45.6 cm; CTDIvol = 32.5 mGy (Body) DLP =
1,482.8 mGy-cm.
   2) Stationary Acquisition 1.0 s, 0.5 cm; CTDIvol = 6.9 mGy (Body) DLP = 3.4
mGy-cm.
   3) Stationary Acquisition 10.0 s, 0.5 cm; CTDIvol = 68.6 mGy (Body) DLP =
34.3 mGy-cm.
   4) Spiral Acquisition 11.6 s, 45.6 cm; CTDIvol = 32.5 mGy (Body) DLP =
1,482.8 mGy-cm.
   5) Spiral Acquisition 3.4 s, 16.6 cm; CTDIvol = 23.9 mGy (Body) DLP = 396.9
mGy-cm.
 Total DLP (Body) = 3,400 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  CTA right lower extremity from ___.

FINDINGS: 

There is a large, complex right thigh hematoma with the largest dimension in
the transverse plane measuring 16.4 cm in the AP plane measuring 13.8 cm. 
Craniocaudal measurement is 20.2 cm.  There is no evidence of active
extravasation within the hematoma.  Right femoral hardware is unchanged since
the prior CT.  With no hardware complication noted.  The imaged portion of the
right hemipelvis is intact.
Enlarged right external iliac lymph node measures 57 x 38 mm, unchanged from
___.  Additionally, an enlarged lymph node in the right thigh (12:52)
measures 23 x 24 mm, similar to the prior study.
No free fluid is noted in the imaged portion of the pelvis or right lower
quadrant.
Imaged bowel loops are normal in caliber.

IMPRESSION:


1. Interval enlargement of the complex right thigh hematoma compared to ___, without evidence of active extravasation.
2. Stable, enlarged right external iliac lymph node.
3. No evidence of hardware related complication.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is ___ man with a high-grade unclassified 
sarcoma (malignant fibrous histiocytoma)
of the right femur s/p radical resection in ___ s/p adjuvant 
doxorubicin and cisplatin x 4 cycles completed ___, now with 
recently diagnosed recurrence in the pelvis and likely in the 
lungs with recurrent hemorrhage into the right leg 
sarcoma/hematoma and previous PE who presented with new 
incidental finding of PE on imaging. 

Pulmonary Embolism: 
- Patient with prior extensive bilateral PE diagnosed in ___ and IVC filter was placed in ___ given his ongoing 
hemorrhage into right thigh hematoma while on lovenox before 
ultimately stopping the lovenox due to persistent bleeding. 
Patient with incidental finding of large PE on follow-up 
imaging. He has been asymptomatic. He was briefly started on IV 
heparin but that was stopped. Troponins negative with mildly 
elevated BNP and no evidence of right heart strain on CT or EKG. 
He is high risk for bleeding while on anticoagulation due to 
ongoing uncontrolled bleeding and concern for compartment 
syndrome in the right lower extremity. Amputation was discussed 
to control ongoing bleeding at sarcoma site which would then 
allow for anticoagulation but this was determined to be a high 
risk in the setting of PEs and unclear benefit given decreased 
life expectancy and the decision was made by orthopedic surgery, 
the patient's primary oncologist and the patient to not proceed. 
The patient does have an IVC filter which placement was 
confirmed with imaging.

Acute Kidney Injury: 
- Likely pre-renal from decreased PO intake. Non-oliguric. 
Improved with IV Fluids.

Hypotension: 
- SBP ___. Patient asymptomatic. Likely due to hypovolemia. 
However on review baseline SPBs recently have been in the 100s. 
Improved with IV fluids.

Metastatic High-Grade Sarcoma of the Bone
- Now with local recurrence and distant mets to the lungs and 
brain. Lung mets had been relatively slow growing, although 
locoregional disease has been quite aggressive. He is s/p 
pallitative radiation to the thigh, although given persistent 
bleeding into hematoma and subsequent pain, he has been followed 
by orthopedics with consideration for radical amputation. No 
further chemotherapy treatment options. Palliative care and 
social work were consulted. A lengthy meeting was held with the 
orthopedic surgery, the patient's primary oncologist, the 
patient, and patient's family. It was decided that at this time 
the risks of an amputation would not outweigh the benefits. 
Given lack of further treatment options the patient has decided 
to transition to hospice care after underling cyberknife 
radiation to his brain metastasis next week. He does wish to 
continue receiving blood transfusions at this time as these 
improve  his quality of life. His current home care agency has a 
hospice agency but they are unable to allow blood transfusions 
so he will likely need to transition to a different hospice 
agency. His primary oncology office will assist with setting 
this up. A MOLST was filled out with the patient prior to 
discharge and he decided to be DNR/DNI.

Anemia/Thigh Hematoma: 
- Patient with known chronic hemorrhage into thigh 
sarcoma/hematoma. Has required significant transfusion support 
and currently receiving weekly blood transfusions at home. He is 
s/p 1 unit pRBCs on ___,  ___, and ___. Currently 
hemodynamically stable.

CNS Lesion: 
- MRI brain with solitary 12 x 8 mm right cerebellar enhancing 
lesion with thin rim of surrounding vasogenic edema concerning 
for metastasis. Currently no neurological symptoms. Discussed 
with Dr. ___ in Neuro ___, not recommending steroids or 
ant-epileptics at this time. He will follow-up with Radiation 
Oncology as an outpatient for stereotactic radiosurgery next 
week.

Cellulitis/Abscess: 
- Patient with chronic cyst on back that is currently 
erythematous, tender and draining purulent fluid. However, 
patient and family reports this has been present for many years 
and will intermittently express pus and never been incised or 
taken antibiotics. Ultrasound showed complex fluid collection. 
Continues to drain from sinus tract. No fevers or elevated WBC. 
Finished 7-day course of Bactrim and Keflex.

Thrombocytopenia: 
- Multifactorial. Currently stable.

Fever
- Isolated fever. No obvious source. Possibly due to disease. 
Blood and urine cultures negative at the time of discharge.

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with IVC filter.  // Please evaluate IVC filter
position.

TECHNIQUE:  Portable supine abdominal radiograph

COMPARISON:  PET-CT dated ___

FINDINGS: 

There are no abnormally dilated loops of large or small bowel.
The IVC filter projects over the right side of the L2 and L3 vertebral bodies.
Osseous structures are unremarkable apart from a right hip hemiarthroplasty.
Mild degenerative changes of the lower lumbar spine.

IMPRESSION: 

The IVC filter projects over the right side of the L2 and L3 vertebral bodies.

EXAMINATION:  MR HEAD W AND W/O CONTRAST T9112 MR HEAD.

INDICATION:  History of metastatic sarcoma with PE and head CT demonstrating
small right cerebellar lesion.  Evaluate for metastatic disease.

TECHNIQUE:  Sagittal and axial T1 weighted imaging were performed. After
administration of 8 mL of Gadavist intravenous contrast, axial imaging was
performed with gradient echo, FLAIR, diffusion, and T1 technique. Sagittal
MPRAGE imaging was performed and re-formatted in axial and coronal
orientations.

COMPARISON:  Noncontrast head CT ___.

FINDINGS: 

Mildly hyperintense lesion in the right cerebellum corresponds to a 12 x 8 mm
enhancing lesion (900:69) with thin rim of surrounding vasogenic edema without
significant associated mass effect.  This lesion demonstrates slowed
diffusion.  There is no associated susceptibility artifact suggest hemorrhagic
transformation.  No additional enhancing lesion is identified.

There is no evidence of hemorrhage, significant mass effect, midline shift or
infarction.   The ventricles and sulci are normal in caliber and configuration
for age.  The principal intracranial vascular flow voids are preserved.  The
dural venous sinuses are patent on MP rage images.

The paranasal sinuses are grossly clear.  The orbits are grossly unremarkable.

IMPRESSION: 

Solitary 12 x 8 mm right cerebellar enhancing lesion with thin rim of
surrounding vasogenic edema corresponding to CT findings, given history
compatible with metastasis.  No evidence of hemorrhagic transformation.  No
additional enhancing lesions.

EXAMINATION:  US, OTHER SOFT TISSUE AREA

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with draining abscess over back  // eval
drainable fluid collection

TECHNIQUE:  Grayscale ultrasound images were obtained of the superficial
tissues of the left upper back.

COMPARISON:  None

FINDINGS: 

Transverse and sagittal images were obtained of the superficial tissues of the
left upper back.  In the area of clinical concern, there is a 2.6 x 3.1 x 0.9
cm predominantly hypoechoic fluid collection with peripheral hyperemia but no
central vascularity.  The collection demonstrates posterior acoustic
enhancement and low level internal echogenicity.  The superficial aspect of
the collection comes to the skin surface, and there is a suggestion draining
sinus tract.  The deep aspect of the collection is confined within the
superficial soft tissues.

IMPRESSION: 

2.6 x 3.1 x 0.9 cm complex fluid collection in the superficial tissues of the
left upper back with a draining sinus tract.   this would be amenable to
aspiration if clinically warranted.

EXAMINATION:  CT HEAD W/O CONTRAST Q111 CT HEAD.

INDICATION:  History: ___ with PE. CT head to r/o metastatic disease prior to
heparin  // ?mets.

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous axial images of the brain were obtained without
contrast. Coronal and sagittal reformations as well as bone algorithm
reconstructions were provided and reviewed.

DOSE:  Acquisition sequence:
   1) Sequenced Acquisition 16.0 s, 16.9 cm; CTDIvol = 47.4 mGy (Head) DLP =
802.7 mGy-cm.
 Total DLP (Head) = 803 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  None.

FINDINGS: 

An 8 mm hyperdensity in the right cerebellum near midline with a small rim of
vasogenic edema is concerning for a focal mass, the possibility of small area
within this lesion associated with hemorrhagic transformation cannot be
completely rule out, correlation with MRI of the head with and without
contrast is recommended for further characterization.  The ventricles and
sulci prominent for the patient's age, suggesting cortical volume loss.

There is no evidence of fracture.  The visualized portion of the paranasal
sinuses, mastoid air cells, and middle ear cavities are clear.  The visualized
portion of the orbits are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:


1. 8 mm hyperdensity in the right cerebellum with associated vasogenic edema
is concerning for a focal mass, possibly metastasis given the clinical
history.

RECOMMENDATION(S):  Focal area of high attenuation identified in the right
cerebellum as described detail above, associated with vasogenic edema,
concerning for focal mass lesion, correlation with MRI of the head with and
without contrast recommended for further characterization.

EXAMINATION:  LUMBAR SPINE MRI WITH AND WITHOUT CONTRAST

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with new lumbar sciatic symptoms,, history of
malignant sarcoma of the right proximal femur status post wide resection with
negative margins and reconstruction, status post chemotherapy.  Evaluate for
metastases to lumbar spine.

TECHNIQUE:  Sagittal T1 weighted, T2 weighted, and IDEAL images of the lumbar
spine with axial T1 and T2 weighted images. Following intravenous gadolinium
administration (8 cc Gadavist), sagittal and axial T1 weighted images were
obtained.

COMPARISON:  ___ FDG tumor imaging.

FINDINGS: 

There are 4 lumbar-type vertebrae and a partially sacralized L5.  Vertebral
body heights are within normal limits.  There is minimal retrolisthesis of L4
on L5.  Bone marrow signal is diffusely heterogenous on T1 and T2 weighted
images, without evidence for focal lesions on fat-suppressed IDEAL images. 
There are extensive discogenic bone marrow changes in the endplates from L2-L3
through L4-L5.

The distal spinal cord appears unremarkable, with the conus medullaris
terminating near the lower aspect of T12.  There is no abnormal intrathecal
contrast enhancement.

T12-L1:  Mild disc bulge and a small central/left paracentral disc protrusion.
No spinal canal narrowing and no significant neural foraminal narrowing.

L1-L2:  Mild bilateral facet arthropathy without spinal canal or neural
foraminal narrowing.

L2-L3:  Disc bulge and moderate facet arthropathy, as well as mild thickening
of the ligamentum flavum.  The subarticular zones are mildly narrowed without
compression of the traversing L3 nerve roots.  The thecal sac is slightly
narrowed without crowding of the intrathecal nerve roots.  There is mild to
moderate right neural foraminal narrowing with abutment of the exiting right
L2 nerve root by a facet osteophyte.  There is no significant left neural
foraminal narrowing.

L3-L4:  There is a disc bulge, larger on the left than right, as well as
thickening of the ligamentum flavum and moderate bilateral facet arthropathy. 
There is moderate spinal canal stenosis with crowding of the intrathecal nerve
roots, as well as abutment of bilateral traversing L4 nerve roots in the
subarticular zones with greater mass effect on the left than right.  There is
also mild to moderate right and mild left neural foraminal narrowing.

L4-L5:  There is a disc bulge, larger on the left than right, thickening of
the ligamentum flavum, and moderate, left greater than right facet
arthropathy.  There is left greater than right subarticular zone narrowing
with abutment of the traversing right L5 nerve root and displacement of the
traversing left L5 nerve root.  There is mild to moderate narrowing of the
thecal sac without significant crowding of the intrathecal nerve roots.  There
is mild to moderate bilateral neural foraminal narrowing.

L5-S1:  The disc and facet joints are underdeveloped due to partial
sacralization of L5.  No spinal canal or neural foraminal narrowing.

1 cm left renal cyst on images 6:9, 9:9 appear simple.

IMPRESSION:


1. 4 lumbar-type vertebrae and a partially sacralized L5.
2. No evidence for an osseous or soft tissue mass in the lumbar spine.
3. Multilevel lumbar degenerative disease, as detailed above, including
moderate spinal canal narrowing at L3-L4, and mild spinal canal narrowing at
L2-L3 and L4-L5.

ADDENDUM  The pathology showed:  Metastatic HCC.
This result is concordant with imaging findings.
Recommendations: no further evaluation of this lesion is indicated.
The meeting was attended by: ___.

EXAMINATION:  CT-GUIDED LEFT ADRENAL MASS BIOPSY

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with cirrhosis/___ p/w adrenal mass on imaging.
Hormonal studies have been negative, concern for HCC met// is this metastatic
or primary adrenal mass (adenoma vs cancer?)

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen and pelvis from ___.

PROCEDURE:  CT-guided left adrenal mass biopsy.

OPERATORS:  Dr. ___, radiology trainee and Dr. ___, attending
radiologist. Dr. ___ personally supervised the trainee during the key
components of the procedure and reviewed and agrees with the trainee's
findings.

TECHNIQUE:  The risks, benefits, and alternatives of the procedure were
explained to the patient.  After a detailed discussion, informed written
consent was obtained.  A pre-procedure timeout using three patient identifiers
was performed per ___ protocol.

The patient was placed in a prone position on the CT scan table.  Limited
preprocedure CTscan of the intended biopsy area was performed.  Based on the
CT findings an appropriate position for the biopsy was chosen.  The site was
marked.

The site was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.  1% lidocaine
were administered to the subcutaneous and deep tissues for local anesthetic
effect.  Under CT guidance, a 17 gauge coaxial needle was introduced into the
lesion.  An 18 gauge core biopsy device with a 22 mm throw was used to obtain
3 core biopsy specimens, which were sent for pathology.

Due to oozing from the needle after biopsy passes (possibly from necrotic
___ adrenal mass) the tract was embolized with Gelfoam slurry while
removing the coaxial introducer.

The procedure was tolerated well and there were no immediate post-procedural
complications.

DOSE:  Acquisition sequence:
   1) Spiral Acquisition 8.8 s, 27.0 cm; CTDIvol = 12.7 mGy (Body) DLP = 332.8
mGy-cm.
   2) Stationary Acquisition 7.2 s, 1.4 cm; CTDIvol = 75.3 mGy (Body) DLP =
108.4 mGy-cm.
 Total DLP (Body) = 452 mGy-cm.

SEDATION:  Moderate sedation was provided by administering divided doses of
2.5 mg Versed and 125 mcg fentanyl throughout the total intra-service time of
25 minutes during which patient's hemodynamic parameters were continuously
monitored by an independent trained radiology nurse.

FINDINGS: 

Large solid mass involving the left adrenal gland, this was targeted for the
core biopsy.  10 mm nonobstructing left renal pelvic stone.  TIPS in place
with cirrhotic liver.  Numerous endovascular embolization coils.

IMPRESSION: 

Successful CT-guided left adrenal mass biopsy.

EXAMINATION:  CT CHEST W/CONTRAST

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with HCV cirrhosis c/b ___ now with new adrenal
mass// Eval for metastases

TECHNIQUE:  Multidetector helical scanning of the chest was reconstructed as
contiguous 5- and 1.25-mm thick axial, 2.5-mm thick coronal and parasagittal,
and 8 x 8 mm MIPs axial images.

DOSE:  Acquisition sequence: 1) Spiral Acquisition 2.5 s, 39.2 cm; CTDIvol =
16.9 mGy (Body) DLP = 663.2 mGy-cm. Total DLP (Body) = 663 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  None.  Correlation was made with CT abdomen pelvis from ___.

FINDINGS: 

NECK, THORACIC INLET, AXILLAE, CHEST WALL: The thyroid gland is homogeneous in
attenuation without focal nodularity.  There is no supraclavicular or axillary
lymphadenopathy by CT size criteria, though axillary lymph nodes are notable
for the number asymmetric right greater than left gynecomastia is noted. 
Otherwise, the imaged soft tissues are unremarkable..

MEDIASTINUM: Multiple sub carinal nodal conglomerate measure up to 2.7 x 1.0
cm.  Lymph nodes at other stations are mildly enlarged, though not
pathologically enlarged by CT size criteria.

HILA: There is no hilar lymphadenopathy by CT size criteria.  Right hilar
lymph node measures up to 9 mm (302:104).

HEART and PERICARDIUM: The heart size is within normal limits.  Moderate
coronary calcifications in minimal aortic valvular calcifications are noted.

PLEURA: There is no pleural effusion or pneumothorax.

LUNG:
PARENCHYMA: Paraseptal and centrilobular emphysema predominantly in the upper
lobes are moderate.  Evaluation of the lower lobes are mildly limited due to
respiratory motion.  Bibasilar ground-glass opacities in the lower lobes
likely represent atelectasis.  Triangular subpleural right lower lobe nodule,
which may represent an intrapulmonary lymph node measures 4 mm (302:87). 
Right lower lobe subpleural nodule measures 2 mm (302:148). Right upper lobe
nodule measure 4 mm (302:81).  Cluster of nodules in the right upper lobe
spanning 5 mm is nonspecific and may represent impacted terminal bronchi
(302:135).

AIRWAYS: The airways are patent to the subsegmental levels.  However, there is
diffuse peribronchial wall thickening, especially in the lower lobes.  In
addition, there is mild bronchiectasis in the lower lobes, likely due to
chronic bronchitis.

VESSELS: The ascending and descending aorta and the main pulmonary arteries
are normal in caliber.  While this exam is not tailored for evaluation of
pulmonary embolism, no central filling defects are seen.

MUSCULOSKELETAL: There is no suspicious osseous lesion concerning for acute
fracture or malignancy.  Endplate sclerosis at T3 and T4 as well as inferior
endplate of T5 likely represent degenerative change.  Mild anterior wedging
deformity at L1 is chronic.

UPPER ABDOMEN: Again seen is heterogeneously enhancing large left adrenal mass
measuring 9.5 x 8.3 cm, better characterized on the CT abdomen from ___.  Other subdiaphragmatic findings, including cirrhotic liver and prior
embolization coils are also better seen on the dedicated multiphasic CT from ___.

IMPRESSION:


1. No definite evidence of metastatic disease in the chest.  cluster of
nodules may be inflammatory/infection.  Nonspecific micro nodules measuring
less than 5 mm in the right upper lobe and right lower lobe as described
above.
2. Moderate paraseptal and centrilobular emphysema predominantly in the upper
lobes.
3. Findings compatible with chronic bronchitis.
4. Cirrhotic liver and left adrenal mass, better characterized on the
multiphasic CT from ___.

EXAMINATION:  DUPLEX DOPP ABD/PEL

INDICATION:  History: ___ with cirrhosis// ascites, portal vein doppler

TECHNIQUE:  Grey scale, color, and spectral Doppler ultrasound images of the
abdomen were obtained.

COMPARISON:  CT from ___.  Ultrasound from ___.  MR from ___..

FINDINGS: 

The liver appears diffusely coarsened and nodular consistent with known
cirrhosis.  A 1.8 x 1.6 x 1.7 cm hypoechoic lesion in the left lobe is again
seen, not significantly changed from prior.  There is an additional hypoechoic
lesion with slightly hypoechoic rim in the left lobe measuring 2.4 x 3.0 x 2.2
cm, which was not seen on prior imaging.  There is no ascites. There is stable
splenomegaly, with the spleen measuring 13.8 cm.  There is no intrahepatic
biliary dilation. The CHD measures 4 mm. Cholelithiasis without gallbladder
wall thickening.  A 9 x 5 x 7 mm hypodensity in the spleen is unchanged from
prior

The main portal vein is patent with hepatopetal flow.
The TIPS is patent and demonstrates wall-to-wall flow.
Portal vein and intra-TIPS velocities are as follows:
Main portal vein: 49 cm/sec, previously 79 cm/sec
Proximal TIPS: 116 cm/sec, previously 160cm/sec
Mid TIPS: 99 cm/sec, previously 81 cm/sec
Distal TIPS: 85 cm/sec, previously 85 cm/sec

Flow within the left portal vein is towards the TIPS shunt. Flow within the
right anterior portal vein is  towards the TIPS.  Appropriate flow is seen in
the hepatic veins and IVC.

PANCREAS: The pancreas is not well visualized, largely obscured by overlying
bowel gas.

KIDNEYS:  Limited views of the kidneys demonstrate no hydronephrosis.

RETROPERITONEUM: Visualized portions of aorta and IVC are within normal
limits.

IMPRESSION: 

1.  Patent TIPS, with stable velocities and appropriate direction of flow.
2.  Stable hypoechoic lesion in the left lobe of the liver.  An additional
hypoechoic lesion with hypoechoic rim measuring 2.4 cm in the left lobe, not
well seen on prior study.

RECOMMENDATION(S):  MRI further evaluation of a hypoechoic lesion in the left
lobe of the liver not well seen on prior study.

Chest:  Frontal and lateral views

INDICATION:  History: ___ with wheeze// pna

TECHNIQUE:  Chest:  Frontal and Lateral

COMPARISON:  ___

FINDINGS: 

The lungs are clear without focal consolidation.  No pleural effusion or
pneumothorax is seen. The cardiac and mediastinal silhouettes are

IMPRESSION: 

No acute cardiopulmonary process.

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with painful desmoid for cryoablation (attn.
Dr. ___  // ___ year old woman with painful desmoid for cryoablation (attn.
Dr. ___

EXAMINATION:  CT-guided cryoablation

COMPARISON:  MRI abdomen and pelvis ___

TECHNIQUE:  OPERATORS: Dr. ___, radiology trainee and Dr. ___
___, attending radiologist. Dr. ___ supervised the trainee
during the key components of the procedure and reviewed and agree with the
trainee's findings.
ANESTHESIA:  General anesthesia was administered by the anesthesiology
department.
MEDICATIONS:  For full details please refer to anesthesiology notes.
CONTRAST: None
RADIATION DOSE: Acquisition sequence:
   1) Spiral Acquisition 9.4 s, 27.0 cm; CTDIvol = 19.7 mGy (Body) DLP = 506.7
mGy-cm.
   2) Spiral Acquisition 6.4 s, 19.5 cm; CTDIvol = 22.1 mGy (Body) DLP = 414.4
mGy-cm.
   3) Stationary Acquisition 2.9 s, 1.4 cm; CTDIvol = 30.1 mGy (Body) DLP =
43.4 mGy-cm.
   4) Spiral Acquisition 6.4 s, 19.5 cm; CTDIvol = 20.7 mGy (Body) DLP = 376.7
mGy-cm.
   5) Stationary Acquisition 1.4 s, 1.4 cm; CTDIvol = 15.1 mGy (Body) DLP =
21.7 mGy-cm.
   6) Spiral Acquisition 19.1 s, 19.5 cm; CTDIvol = 57.2 mGy (Body) DLP =
1,042.9 mGy-cm.
   7) Spiral Acquisition 25.5 s, 19.5 cm; CTDIvol = 76.1 mGy (Body) DLP =
1,387.1 mGy-cm.
 Total DLP (Body) = 3,805 mGy-cm.

PROCEDURE:  PROCEDURE DETAILS:

Following explanation of the risks, benefits and alternatives to the
procedure, written informed consent was obtained from the patient. The patient
was then brought to the computed tomography suite and placed supine on the
imaging table.  General anesthesia was induced by the anesthesiologist. 
Following
scout imaging, the skin was marked and draped in the usual sterile fashion.

Under ultrasound and CT fluoroscopy, four 3.8 mm and two 2.4 mm cryoprobes
were placed in a parallel orientation along the long axis of the tumor from a
lateral to medial approach spaced approximately 2 cm apart and extending close
to the medial margin of the tumor.  15 minutes of freezing followed by 10
minutes following and an additional 15 minutes of freezing was performed.  The
cryoprobes were pulled back approximately 5 cm and this more proximal portion
of the tumor was treated in the same fashion.  2 of the probes were turned off
during portions of freezing as freezing was adequately achieved along these
margins.

Post procedural computed tomography demonstrated a large iceball occupying
approximately 70% of the tumor volume.  The skin was then cleaned and a dry
sterile dressing was applied. The patient was awakened from general anesthesia
without incident and there were no immediate post-procedure complications. The
patient was transferred to the post-anesthesia care unit
for further monitoring.

FINDINGS: 

Re- demonstrated is a large mass within the right lower quadrant measuring up
to 14 cm compatible with the patient's known biopsy-proven desmoid tumor.  No
other intra-abdominal or intrapelvic abnormalities are seen.

IMPRESSION: 

CT-guided cryoablation of a large abdominal desmoid tumor.  It is estimated
that 70% of the tumor volume was ablated.

RECOMMENDATION(S):  The patient is scheduled to return for cryoablation of the
residual tumor in 3 weeks.

Ms. ___ is a ___ G6P3 with a h/o T1DM admitted with 
poor glycemic control, also s/p left sided flank impact from car 
accident while walking. She was admitted to the antepartum unit. 
On admission, her anion gap was 16 which down trended to 10. She 
was started on levemir 14 units QHS and Humalog SSI. She was 
also complaining of left flank pain on admission. However, there 
were no clinical signs of abruption and ultrasound (___) was 
reassuring. She underwent fetal testing that was reassuring. 

Patient was advised to remain in the hospital for 24 hours of 
observation, but she elected to leave against medical advice. 
She was counseled on the risks of poor glycemic control and 
preterm labor and given return precautions. She was subsequently 
discharged home against medical advice, with outpatient 
follow-up scheduled.

Dear Ms. ___,

You were admitted to the hospital with poorly controlled Type 1 
diabetes, and monitoring after a motor vehicle accident. All of 
your fetal testing have been reassuring. You were restarted on 
your home insulin regimen. You had an ultrasound which was 
reassuring. We recommend that you stay in the hospital for 24 
hours of monitoring, however you elected to leave against 
medical advice tonight. Please follow the instructions below:  
 - Attend all appointments with your obstetrician and all fetal 
scans  
 - Monitor for the following danger signs:  
 - headache that is not responsive to medication  
 - abdominal pain  
 - increased swelling in your legs  
 - vision changes  
 - Worsening, painful or regular contractions  
 - Vaginal bleeding  
 - Leakage of water or concern that your water broke  
 - Nausea/vomiting  
 - Fever, chills  
 - Decreased fetal movement  
 - Other concerns
